required_concepts: Discrete data is countable and has distinct categories with no in-between values
Age in years is recorded as whole numbers without fractions
optional_concepts: Examples of discrete measurement: 25 years old vs 25.5 years old
Contextual use of decimal precision in age measurement
acceptable_paraphrases: Distinct categories with no intermediate values
critical_errors: Ignoring the standard practice of whole-number recording
misconceptions: Believing age can be measured with decimal precision in all contexts
Confusing discrete with continuous due to potential fractional measurements
grading_notes: Accept discrete/continuous debate but prioritize standard statistical classification. Penalize for ignoring whole-number recording convention.
